docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Authors create or edit markdown files in the docs/ folder
  2. A Pull Request is opened for review
  3. A preview deployment is generated automatically for verification
  4. Once merged, the site is published to GitHub Pages

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Markdown-based - Write content in familiar markdown syntax
  • Full-text search - Find any document instantly with client-side search
  • Auto-navigation - Site structure mirrors the folder hierarchy
  • Preview deployments - Review changes before they go lives

docs.title: Central Entity: CORE_USER
docs.text:
The CORE_USER table (PK: idst) is the hub of the entire data model. Nearly all domains reference it via an iduser foreign key. When building analytics queries, joins to CORE_USER provide:

  • User identity and profile fields
  • Branch/group membership (via CORE_GROUP_MEMBERS)
  • Role assignments (via CORE_ROLE_MEMBERS)
  • Manager relationships (via CORE_ORG_CHART_TREE)

docs.title: Usage Notes
docs.text:
• No declared FKs: DM_* tables are denormalized — they embed dimension data directly rather than joining via foreign keys.
  • Best for reporting: Use these tables as the primary source for dashboards and analytics. They avoid complex multi-table joins.
  • DM_ENROLLMENTS (93 columns) is the most comprehensive single table for enrollment analytics.
  • DM_USERS (128 columns) includes all custom user fields, branch hierarchy, and computed attributes.
  • Refresh frequency: These are typically refreshed on a scheduled basis (not real-time).

docs.title: Contributing to Cerebro
docs.text: This guide explains how to add, edit, and publish knowledge articles in Cerebro.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Git access to this repository
  • A text editor that supports markdown (VS Code, etc.)

docs.title: Local Development
docs.text:
To preview the site locally:

pip install -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve

The site will be available at http://127.0.0.1:8000.

docs.title: Create a New Article
docs.text:
1. Create a markdown file under docs/:
  2. For a new topic area, create a subdirectory: docs/my-topic/index.md

  3. For a page within an existing topic: docs/existing-topic/my-page.md

  4. Add a YAML front matter header (optional): 

    ---
title: My Article Title
---

  5. Write your content using standard markdown.

docs.title: Add Images
docs.text:
1. Place image files in docs/assets/
  2. Reference them with relative paths in your markdown: 
    ![Alt text](../assets/my-image.png)

docs.title: Update Navigation
docs.text:
If you want explicit control over page ordering, edit the nav section in mkdocs.yml:

nav:
  - Home: index.md
  - Getting Started: getting-started/index.md
  - My New Section: my-topic/index.md

If omitted from nav, pages are still accessible via search and direct URL but won't appear in the sidebar.

docs.title: 1. Create a Branch
docs.text: git checkout -b docs/my-new-article

docs.title: 2. Write Your Content
docs.text: Add or edit files under docs/. Use mkdocs serve locally to preview.

docs.title: 3. Open a Pull Request
docs.text: Push your branch and open a PR against main.

docs.title: 4. Review the Preview
docs.text:
Once the PR is opened, a GitHub Action automatically builds and deploys a preview. Look for the bot comment on your PR with a link like:

https://<org>.github.io/<repo>/preview/pr-<number>/

Use this to verify formatting, images, and navigation before merging.

docs.title: 5. Merge
docs.text: Once approved, merge the PR. The deploy workflow will automatically: - Build the site - Publish to GitHub Pages - Update the search index - Clean up the preview deployment

docs.title: File Organization
docs.text:
docs/
├── index.md              # Site homepage
├── assets/               # Images and static files
├── topic-a/
│   ├── index.md          # Topic landing page
│   └── subtopic.md       # Detailed sub-page
└── topic-b/
    └── index.md

docs.title: Markdown Features
docs.text:
Cerebro supports these markdown extensions:

Feature Syntax Admonitions !!! note "Title" Code highlighting Fenced blocks with language tag Table of contents Auto-generated from headings Permalink anchors Auto-added to all headings

docs.title: Search
docs.text: The site includes full-text client-side search powered by Lunr.js. The search index is rebuilt automatically on every deployment. No configuration is needed — all published pages are indexed.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Solution Preview not appearing Check the Actions tab for build errors Images not loading Verify relative path from the markdown file to assets/ Page not in navigation Add it to the nav section in mkdocs.yml Build fails with --strict Fix any broken links or missing references

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide covers how to add and manage content in Cerebro.

docs.title: Adding a New Document
docs.text:
1. Create a new .md file under the docs/ directory
  2. Organize files into subdirectories by topic
  3. Open a Pull Request with your changes

docs.title: Adding Images
docs.text:
Place image files in docs/assets/ and reference them with relative paths:

![Description](../assets/my-image.png)

docs.title: Markdown Features
docs.text: Cerebro supports standard markdown plus these extensions:

docs.title: Admonitions
docs.text:
Note

Use admonitions to call out important information.

Warning

Warnings highlight potential issues.

docs.text: print("Syntax highlighting is supported")

docs.text:

│   └── images go here
├── topic-a/
│   ├── index.md
